what: Agents in flight, and why. A finished agent is REMOVED from this file, not marked done — the page shows what is happening now, and history lives in git.

agents.what: Two thirds of the time we already show a cousin of the right fund
agents.why: We measured where the right fund sits when we miss it, and the answer changed the plan. In 63% of misses the founder is already looking at a SIBLING of the fund they would have won — same programme, wrong door. So we are not sending people to the wrong place; we are picking the wrong door in the right place. The question now is whether a fact that tells two doors apart even exists: in our data, on the funder's own page, or only in the founder's head. If it mostly does not exist, that caps what this product can promise and you need to know.

agents.what: Three of our eleven sectors are missing from the corpus
agents.why: Our own safety check caught it: the corpus we run on now holds eight top-level sectors where it held eleven, and the snapshot the site falls back on still says eleven. This matters more than housekeeping, because sector is one of the two things our ranking scores a fund on — the same ranking the other two agents are working. If a quarter of that resolution went missing, every ordering measurement since is standing on it. The job is to say what happened, when, whether it was a deliberate tidy-up or a loss, and what it cost.
